ai_suggestion: Do not use the top-1 AudioSet label: generic parents (Animal, Vehicle, Speech) win top-1, e.g. dog clips -> 'Animal'. Hand-picked specific labels per class, score = max over them, argmax over 50 classes. Accuracy 80.1% overall, 85.2% on mappable classes. Mapping in src/label_map.py, prediction table in notebook.

goal: Mapping rule for labels shared by two classes
ai_suggestion: Each AudioSet label belongs to at most one class. 'Chicken, rooster' and 'Fowl' are dropped, so hen = Cluck and rooster = Crowing. Otherwise hen and rooster get identical scores and the hen/rooster confusion would come from the mapping, not the model. Same for Insect, Vehicle, Aircraft, Water, Liquid, Door, Alarm.

drinking_sipping, can_opening, washing_machine have no matching label and can never be predicted (0% by construction). Options: keep them and report separately (mappable flag), drop them from accuracy, or pick nearest labels. Default in code: keep + mappable column.

goal: Does the baseline support the research question (animal confusions)?
ai_suggestion: On clean ESC-50 animals are 99% correct, hen vs rooster has 1 error. Most baseline confusions are water/mechanical/human sounds (pouring_water->water_drops, washing_machine->engine, mouse_click->keyboard). The animal story needs perturbations/mixing to produce confusions, or the question should be widened.

goal: Definition of 'animal' for the animal vs non-animal question
ai_suggestion: ESC-50 puts chirping_birds and crickets under 'natural soundscapes' although they are animal sounds; the model scores them as animal (p_animal_max 0.44 / 0.39). Decide whether 'animal' follows ESC-50 categories or biology.

AudioSet parent 'Animal' is inconsistent with its children: cow has p(Animal)=0.01 while Moo=0.89, frog 0.05 vs Frog 0.87. Proposed two scores: p_animal_parent and p_animal_max (max over all animal labels). Possible Phase I finding about the model's class hierarchy, link to Phase II embeddings.
why: Good idea for later, keep both columns for Phase II

goal: Check handover summary claims against results
prompt: Summary for teammates: 1) lyrebird mostly classified as bird but confusion bigger than ESC-50; 2) model can't distinguish human imitations from real animals; 3) perturbations confuse the model. Is everything correct?
ai_suggestion: Checked CSVs: (1) 133/159 lyrebird windows -> chirping_birds, no siren/car alarm/chainsaw detected; 'bigger confusion than ESC-50' not measurable without per-window ground truth. (2) Mixed, n=8: 4 imitations scored as the imitated animal (bees, angry chicken, pig weakly, sheep 0.74 at the end), 4 recognised as human (Whistling, Snicker, Humming, Speech).
